facts.text: Serve the tea when Mrs Mills brings in the tray.
facts.why: Mrs Mills is the housekeeper and serves the family, but none of the sources opened (Wikipedia, Wikiquote, a plot explainer) describe a scene where she brings in a tea tray.
facts.fix: Serve the tea when Mrs Mills first arrives at the house looking for work.

facts.text: Supper by candlelight again, children. Mind the curtains, finish your potatoes, and no talking to anyone you can't see.
facts.why: Grace never says this. Her real lines include 'No one can make us leave this house.' and 'This house is ours.'
facts.fix: No one can make us leave this house.

fix_note.text: No one can make us leave this house.

facts.text: Sleep tight. Mrs Mills checks the curtains twice.
facts.why: It is Grace who is strict about the curtains. The sources say the curtains vanish one morning and Mrs Mills and Tuttle seem unbothered. Nothing shows Mrs Mills checking them twice.
facts.fix: Sleep tight. Grace checks the curtains twice.

facts.text: The ring of keys at Grace's belt
facts.why: The film does stress that doors are opened one at a time and closed behind, but no source opened mentions Grace's key ring. The menu's 'Every door locked' lines lean on it too.
facts.fix: The doors closed one at a time behind Grace

vibe.verdict: Dark, quiet manor look with sound 1945 British food, but a room service layout fits a hotel better than a haunted house and the best scares are left out.
